conventions.convention: D is bounded and Lebesgue measurable, q is an essentially bounded complex class extended by zero, and k is real. The equation is u=f+K_k u with G_k(z)=exp(ik|z|)/(4π|z|), G_k(0)=0, and distributional sign (−Δ−k²)(u−f)=qu. Null domains give the zero L2 space.
The far-field amplitude is (4π)⁻¹ times the integral of exp(−ikθ·y)q(y)v(y), corresponding to the exterior factor exp(ikr)/r.

H_ell consists of restrictions of homogeneous harmonic complex polynomials of degree ell; −Δ_S² has eigenvalue ell(ell+1), surface measure has mass 4π, and the zonal polynomial has P_ell(1)=1. Degrees start at zero.

The discretization uses nested dyadic cell averages and K_N=P_NK_k. Matrix weights integrate entire cell pairs exactly, including diagonal pairs; normalized indicators give the matrix basis. No point sampling or approximate-weight certificate is asserted.
The Born partial sum indexed by m≥0 includes powers j=0 through m. Its hypothesis is operator norm strictly below one.

The radial reduction assumes k,R>0, continuous complex radial contrast, regular-origin total modes, explicit incident regular-mode forms, interface continuity of the field and radial derivative, and a uniform outgoing radiation condition. It is conditional and asserts no total-field existence or uniqueness.

Countable Choice suffices for the boundedness and Born branches; the compactness and Fredholm branches explicitly assume full AC. Harmonic completeness and the radial branch carry Countable Choice and Dependent Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let D have finite Lebesgue measure. For every product-measurable kernel a∈L2(D×D;C), the integral formula defines a representative-independent complex-linear map L2(D;C)→L2(D;C) with ||T_a||≤||a||_L2. For the bounded-domain scattering model, ||K_k||≤||q||∞ sqrt(|D| diam(D)/(4π)).
Assume AC and the data of def-volume-integral-scattering-model with 0<|D|<∞. Then K_k:L2(D;C)→L2(D;C) is compact and ||K_k||≤||G_k(x−y)q(y)||_L2(D×D)≤||q||∞ sqrt(|D| diam(D)/(4π)).

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Each H_ell has complex dimension 2ell+1; these spaces are pairwise orthogonal with dense algebraic sum in L2(S²). Their reproducing kernel is Z_ell(ω,η)=(2ell+1)P_ell(ω·η)/(4π), and |g(ω)|≤sqrt((2ell+1)/(4π))||g||_L2 for g∈H_ell.

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded measurable D and nested dyadic partitions of a containing positive-side half-open cube, cell averaging gives orthogonal projections P_N onto increasing cell-constant spaces V_N, with ||P_N||≤1 and P_Nv→v in L2(D;C) for every v.

Assume Countable Choice and the volume model with 0<|D|<∞. The far-field map is linear into C(S²;C), has norm at most ||q||∞ sqrt(|D|)/(4π), is Lipschitz in direction, and is the uniform far-field limit with the stated O(1/r) bound for r≥2R_0.

Assume Countable Choice. For real k, Φ_k(x)=exp(ik|x|)/(4π|x|) satisfies (−Δ−k²)Φ_k=δ_0 distributionally. For bounded-support g∈L1(R³), its convolution integral exists absolutely almost everywhere, defines an L1_loc function V, and satisfies (−Δ−k²)V=g.
Under AC and the volume model with 0<|D|<∞, injectivity of I−K_k gives a unique solution for every L2 forcing and a bounded inverse A_k⁻¹. Every v satisfies ||u−v||₂≤||A_k⁻¹|| ||f−(I−K_k)v||₂.

Assume Countable Choice and the volume model with 0<|D|<∞. If ρ=||K_k||<1, every forcing has a unique solution, and for m≥0 its Born partial sum u_m=Σ_{j=0}^m K_k^j f satisfies ||u−u_m||₂≤ρ^(m+1)||f||₂/(1−ρ).

concerns.concern: Fact F2 states the operator estimate ||K_k||≤||q||∞ sqrt(|D| diam(D)/(4π)) but cites only lem-three-dimensional-scattering-kernel-is-square-integrable. That lemma states the kernel L2 estimate, not the operator estimate. The missing inequality ||K_k||≤||a||₂ is proved in lem-volume-integral-operator-well-defined-and-bounded, so the example's calculation and conclusion are sound, but the displayed citation overstates its immediate supplier.
